title: Slow and Full
about: Find what is slowing a device down, and free up space safely.

cards.prompt: Your laptop has been getting slower all afternoon. It's probably not broken: one part is struggling. [[RAM]], [[storage]] or the [[CPU]]? Let's find out.

steps.text: What do you do first? (The [[task manager]] shows what every app is using.)

choices.text: Open the task manager to see what's busy

choices.consequence: Booster apps rarely help, and some are junk or worse. Find the cause first.
That's a very expensive way to close 30 tabs. Find the cause first.

steps.text: The task manager shows **RAM 97% full**. You have **30 [[browser]] tabs** open. What's the simplest fix?

choices.text: Close the tabs you don't need
choices.consequence: Each tab uses RAM. With fewer open, the laptop speeds up. Check: it's working!

choices.text: Delete some photos to make room
choices.consequence: Photos are in storage. The problem was RAM, so nothing changes.

cards.explanation: Look first, then fix. The task manager showed **full RAM**, so the fix was closing tabs. Deleting files only frees **storage**, which wasn't the problem.
cards.hint: Before you fix anything, find out what's actually busy. Then match the fix to the part that's full.

cards.title: The fix-it loop
cards.body:
Good fixers use a simple loop:

1. **Describe** exactly what's wrong. "It's broken" is a complaint. "It's slow when 30 [[tabs|browser-tab]] are open" is a clue.
2. **Guess** the most likely cause.
3. **Try** the simplest, safest fix first.
4. **Check** whether it worked. If not, guess again.

cards.prompt: Your friend's laptop crawls whenever lots of tabs are open. Put the fix-it loop in order for this problem.

items.label: Notice it's slow only with lots of tabs open
Guess that the RAM is full
Close the tabs you don't need

cards.explanation: **Describe, guess, try, check.** Spotting *when* it's slow gives the clue, the clue points to RAM, closing tabs is the simple fix, and checking tells you if it worked. If not, you'd go back and guess again.
cards.hint: You can't guess a cause until you've described the problem, and you can't check a fix you haven't tried yet.
cards.nudge: Each step needs the one before it. Start with what you notice, and end with seeing if it worked.

cards.prompt: A laptop breathes through its vents. If the [[CPU]] gets too hot, it **slows itself down** to stay safe. This is called **throttling**.

steps.text: You're watching videos with the laptop on your duvet. Only two tabs are open, and there's plenty of free storage. The fan roars, then everything slows down. What's going on?

choices.text: The duvet blocks the vents, so the CPU gets hot and slows down
choices.consequence: Yes. The heat can't escape, so the CPU throttles.

choices.text: The two tabs have filled the RAM, so the laptop slows down
choices.consequence: Two tabs use only a little RAM. Listen to the clue: the fan is roaring.

choices.text: The videos are filling up storage, so the laptop slows down
choices.consequence: There's plenty of free storage, so that's not it. What does a roaring fan tell you?

choices.text: Move it onto a hard, flat table so the vents are clear
choices.consequence: Air flows again, the CPU cools, and it speeds back up.

choices.text: Put it in the fridge for a few minutes to cool it fast
choices.consequence: Sudden cold can make water droplets form inside. Let it cool slowly in open air instead.

choices.text: Close all your tabs to cool it down
choices.consequence: Only two tabs were open, so that changes very little. The duvet is still blocking the vents, so the heat can't get out.

cards.explanation: A roaring fan and a sudden slowdown point to **heat**. Soft things like duvets and cushions block the vents, so the CPU **throttles** (slows itself down) to stay safe. A hard, flat surface lets it breathe.
cards.hint: Use the clues: few tabs, plenty of storage, and a roaring fan. Which part does the fan cool down?

cards.prompt: This phone is completely full. Free up at least **15 [[GB|gigabyte]]**. Delete big things that are **backed up** or that you **never use**, but **keep your photos and your essay**.
cards.explanation: Big things you don't need are the quickest wins. The game plus the old setup files (left over from installing apps) free 15 GB, and so do the backed-up videos on their own. Photos and the essay were never in danger.
cards.hint: Look for big things you don't need: files that are [[backed up|backup]], or things you never use. Watch the free space meter as you go.
cards.nudge: Photos and the essay must stay. Pick big items that are backed up or unused, and keep going until the free space meter reaches the goal.

cards.prompt: Tidying up [[storage]]. Delete things that are backed up, **duplicated** or unused. Keep your **only copies**, anything you still need, and **system files** (the device needs them to run). Sort each one.

items.label: Setup files for apps already installed
An app you haven't opened in a year
Five blurry copies of the same photo
Your only copy of family photos

cards.explanation: Delete things that are **backed up, duplicated or unused** (an unused app can be installed again later). Keep anything that's your **only copy**, anything you still need, and any **system file**: deleting those can stop the device working.
cards.hint: Ask of each one: is it backed up, a duplicate or unused? Or is it your only copy, still needed, or a system file?
cards.nudge: Only copies, things you still need and system files are risky to delete. Backed-up, duplicated or unused things are the safe ones.

cards.prompt: Your laptop takes five minutes to start, then crawls for a while after.

steps.text: The [[task manager]] has a **Startup** list with **15 apps** that open by themselves when the laptop switches on. What's the likely cause?

choices.text: Too many apps starting at once
choices.consequence: Yes. They all fight for the [[CPU]] and [[RAM]] just as you're trying to start.

choices.text: The screen is set too bright
choices.consequence: Brightness affects the battery, not how fast the laptop starts.

choices.text: Stop the apps you don't need from starting
choices.consequence: They still work when you open them. They just don't all start at once.

choices.text: Stop the antivirus (the security app) from starting
choices.consequence: That's the one to keep. It protects you from the moment you log in.

choices.text: Delete the system files that load first
choices.consequence: Then the laptop might not start at all.

cards.explanation: **Startup apps** open by themselves when the device switches on. Turning off the ones you don't need makes starting up faster. Keep security software running, and never delete system files.
cards.hint: The clue is the **Startup** list. What happens when lots of apps all try to open at the same moment? And which app protects you?

cards.prompt: An [[update]] needs **12 [[GB|gigabyte]] free**. Make room without losing anything that **isn't saved somewhere else**.
cards.explanation: Music is in the cloud, the videos are backed up, and maps can be downloaded again, so deleting those three frees enough. The photos and notes are your **only copies**, so they stay.
cards.hint: Read each label closely. Anything saved somewhere else, or that you can download again, can go. An **only copy** can't.
cards.nudge: Files marked **only copy** have to stay. Look for the ones that say they're also in [[the cloud|cloud]], [[backed up|backup]], or can be downloaded again.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- Use the loop: **describe, guess, try, check**.
- **Slow?** Too many [[tabs|browser-tab]] fill [[RAM]]. Heat makes the CPU slow down.
- **Full?** Delete what's backed up or unused. Keep your only copies.
